implementation_notes: Modern default: the container-injected IMessenger owns recipient registries keyed by message type and optional channel token; WeakReferenceMessenger is the leak-safe default and ObservableRecipient unsubscribes on deactivation. Use WeakReferenceMessenger for view models whose lifetime is managed by the UI, and StrongReferenceMessenger on hot paths where explicit Unregister discipline is guaranteed.
pitfalls: With WeakReferenceMessenger, a recipient that only the messenger references is collected and quietly stops receiving - keep a real owner or use the strong variant.
Request messages throw when no recipient replies, so a missing handler surfaces as an exception at send time.

variants.name: Prism IEventAggregator + PubSubEvent
variants.implementation_notes: Classic MVVM framework realization: IEventAggregator lazily builds one PubSubEvent<TPayload> per event type; Subscribe takes a ThreadOption (publisher/background/UI thread), a keepSubscriberReferenceAlive flag and a Predicate filter, and returns a SubscriptionToken for selective removal. Choose it in Prism-based shells where the aggregator is already a container service and thread marshalling for the UI thread matters.
pitfalls: The default weak delegate reference makes high-frequency publishes slower; keepSubscriberReferenceAlive=true is faster but then every subscriber must unsubscribe on disposal.
ThreadOption.UIThread only works when the aggregator itself was created on the UI thread.
Do not mutate the published payload from a callback - several subscribers may see it concurrently.
